newsitem.title: UK: Man sees slightly higher 1997/98 EU beet sowings.
newsitem.headline: Man sees slightly higher 1997/98 EU beet sowings.

text.p: The area sown to sugar beet in the European Union (EU) should total 2.05 million hectares in 1997/98, just 1.2 percent up on 2.03 million in 1996/97, trade house E D & F Man said on Tuesday.
The changes in planted areas varied were mixed, with significant gains forecast for Greece and Italy which were offset by declines in Spain and Denmark.
Man said the higher yields in 1996/97 had prompted farmers in some member states to decrease their sowing areas marginally.

"The estimated increases in area in Italy and also in Greece and Sweden have outwieghed the smalle downward adjustments to result in a projected area just marginally higher than last season," Man said.
"It would seem unlikely, though certainly not impossible, that last year's high yields will be repeated for a second successive season," it added.
Italy, for example, was expected to increase its beet sowing area as farmers who had previously been attracted by higher returns from grains were set to return to beet.
Man forecast the Italian sowing area at 275,000 hectares for the 1997 beet crop, up more than 11 percent from the 248,000 reported last year.
In Greece, which is expected to show the largest percentage increase in area -- from 40,000 to 50,000 hectares -- the crop outlook was not promising on account of the widespread European drought.
Sowing areas in France and Germany, the trading bloc's two largest sugar producers, were expected to remain little changed for the 1997 crop at 422,000 and 517,000 hectares respectively.
